key_insight: Learning physically interpretable fractional-step operators separately improves fluid-flow rollout accuracy over a single full-step neural operator.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers fast CFD surrogates for varying geometries, with inference approximately 1,000× faster per step than the Monte Carlo solver at comparable error levels.
method: Decompose time evolution into fractional steps and train separate operators using intermediate solver states.
Use conditional-linear Fourier neural operators to preserve linear state mappings while conditioning nonlinearly on inputs such as geometry.
Apply symmetry sampling and corrective cycling to reduce autoregressive error accumulation.
evidence_signal: Across 2D and 3D flows with varying geometries and initial conditions, the full model reduces mean relative L2 rollout error by 68% and 40%, respectively, versus a single full-step neural operator.
watch_item: Training requires access to intermediate fractional-step solver states; generalization beyond the evaluated flow and geometry settings remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Neural Operator Splitting for Fluid Dynamics in Complex Geometry
